title: Superbuy Domestic Tracking: Seller Dispatch to Warehouse Arrival
dek: Follow a Superbuy order from seller dispatch to warehouse intake, separate domestic tracking from international shipping, and document delays clearly.

sections.heading: Read the shipment stage before reading the tracking number
paragraphs: Superbuy domestic tracking concerns the journey from the seller to the warehouse. International parcel tracking concerns a later shipment from the warehouse toward your delivery address. A number associated with the first journey should not be interpreted as evidence that your international parcel has departed. Start by opening the exact shopping order, checking its current stage and identifying which journey the displayed information describes.

The official Shopping Agent guide separates purchase, warehouse inspection and international parcel submission. This article turns that sequence into a practical tracking record. It does not promise a universal seller dispatch time or warehouse processing deadline. The useful question is which event has actually happened, what evidence supports it, and what action remains possible at that stage.

sections.heading: Keep the three identifiers separate
paragraphs: Create separate fields for the shopping order number, the seller's domestic carrier reference and the later international parcel number. Record the carrier name beside each tracking reference where available. A shopping order identifier is useful in an enquiry, but it is not necessarily a carrier tracking code. Likewise, one international parcel can contain several stored orders, so the two records need a deliberate connection.

Also save the selected variant and quantity. Similar shoes in two sizes can produce almost identical order titles, making a correct tracking update easy to attach to the wrong item. Use a row for each order or clearly distinguish the individual items within it. When a seller sends an order in separate packages, record each observed package reference rather than assuming the first delivered package contains everything.

sections.heading: Distinguish label creation from carrier movement
paragraphs: A tracking number can appear before a meaningful carrier scan. Treat the existence of a number as one recorded event, and a collection or movement scan as another. Do not convert a label-created message into a claim that the parcel is already moving. Copy the exact displayed wording into your notes, together with the date you checked it, instead of rewriting every unfamiliar status as shipped.

A tracking page with no visible updates can have several explanations. Information may not yet be available, the carrier may not match the code, or the seller may still need to complete dispatch. These are possibilities to investigate, not diagnoses. Check that the number was copied without spaces or missing characters, confirm the named carrier, and ask the purchasing agent which event the order record actually confirms.

sections.heading: Use a compact domestic tracking log
paragraphs: A useful log has five fields: check time, information source, exact status, supporting reference and next action. The source could be the shopping order screen, a seller message or the domestic carrier record. Keep the original timestamp shown by that source as well as your own check time. Different screens may use different time zones or update at different moments, so a few hours of apparent disagreement need interpretation.

For example, imagine an order that shows a carrier reference on Monday, a collection scan on Tuesday and delivery on Thursday. These are three distinct milestones in an illustrative workflow, not a normal delivery-time promise. Your notes should preserve that distinction. If the warehouse item does not yet appear, the next action is to reconcile the delivery evidence with intake, not to look for an international flight.

sections.heading: Treat delivered and stored as separate checkpoints
paragraphs: A domestic delivery scan and a completed warehouse record describe different things. The scan concerns the carrier's delivery event; the warehouse record connects received goods with your account and the available inspection information. A delivered message alone does not establish that the correct color, size or quantity was received. It also does not prove that the item is ready for your chosen international shipping route.

When intake appears, compare the stored order identifier, quantity and visible variant against your original purchase record. Open the available warehouse photos and note any unresolved question. If carrier delivery is visible but the order is not reconciled, prepare the order number, carrier reference, delivery timestamp and relevant screenshot for an enquiry. Avoid declaring a package lost from the gap alone; ask for its current reconciliation status.

sections.heading: Handle split shipments and mixed orders carefully
paragraphs: One seller may ship multiple items together, while another order may arrive in separate packages. Do not infer the contents from the size of a tracking update or the first warehouse photo. List what was ordered, what each visible package reference covers if known, and what the warehouse has recorded. An unknown association should stay unknown until the seller or agent clarifies it.

Consider an illustrative two-item order in which one garment is stored and a second has no intake record. There are several questions to resolve: whether both were dispatched, whether the same domestic number covers both, and whether the warehouse record is complete. Sending one enquiry with those facts is clearer than opening conflicting requests that describe the entire order as both delivered and missing. Keep replies attached to the same timeline.

sections.heading: Send an enquiry that identifies the missing event
paragraphs: A useful enquiry can be short: identify the shopping order, the selected item, the domestic reference, the latest recorded event and the decision you need. For instance, ask whether a delivery scan has been matched to the warehouse order, or whether the seller has provided a dispatch reference. These requests give the agent a specific fact to investigate without asking them to infer your concern from several unrelated screenshots.

Use the currently available order-enquiry controls. Superbuy's Shopping Agent guidance identifies order enquiry as a way to communicate during purchasing. If an action label or eligibility differs in your account, follow the live process and request clarification. Do not repeatedly submit contradictory cancellation and dispatch instructions. Decide whether your immediate goal is information, a dispatch update or an enquiry about cancellation eligibility, and state that goal plainly.

sections.heading: Connect tracking with the parcel plan
paragraphs: Domestic progress matters because the rest of a planned haul may already be in storage. Record which items are waiting, their displayed storage deadlines and whether delaying the whole group still makes sense. This is a planning comparison, not a reason to demand an impossible delivery promise. You may decide to wait for a confirmed dispatch, reassess the late item or compare a separate parcel for goods already ready.

Do not assume that adding one more item will make international shipping cheaper. The eventual parcel depends on packaging, dimensions, restrictions and currently available routes. When an item reaches storage, update the parcel plan using the actual warehouse information. Keep product decisions and shipping estimates connected, but preserve the difference between a seller's domestic delivery and the international service you have not yet selected.

sections.heading: Close the domestic record with an evidence check
paragraphs: Before marking domestic tracking complete, confirm that the order association is correct, expected quantities are accounted for and the available intake evidence has been reviewed. Record any unresolved variant, damage or measurement question separately. Completion of the domestic journey is a logistics milestone; it is not a quality certificate or approval to ship every received item immediately.

Then link the stored order to the later international parcel when one is created. Keep both histories so a future question can be directed to the correct stage. Your final record should make it possible to explain, in a few sentences, what you bought, when dispatch was evidenced, when delivery was recorded, how intake was reconciled and what remains undecided. That is more useful than repeatedly refreshing a number without knowing which event you are waiting for. Keep this record until the item and its later parcel have been reconciled, so the correct reference remains available if a question arises.

title: Superbuy Returns and Refunds: Steps, Evidence and Costs
dek: Prepare a Superbuy return, cancellation or refund enquiry with the correct order stage, clear evidence and a breakdown of the money involved.

sections.heading: Start with the order stage and the requested outcome
paragraphs: A Superbuy refund enquiry should begin with two facts: where the order is in its journey and what you want to happen next. Cancelling an uncompleted purchase, returning an item already stored at the warehouse and requesting help after international delivery are different situations. A button labelled refund does not by itself tell you which costs are recoverable or whether the seller will accept the request.

Use this guide as a preparation method, not a promise of eligibility. Superbuy's public help resources separate purchasing, parcel logistics and after-sales assistance. Your live order, the source marketplace, the seller's conditions and the particular service determine the available process. Preserve the exact status and any displayed deadline before sending an enquiry. If the account instructions are unclear, ask the agent to identify the applicable route for that specific order.

sections.heading: Build a small evidence packet
paragraphs: Save the shopping order number, seller listing, selected variant, quantity and purchase confirmation. Add the date the issue was noticed and the current order status. For a visible mismatch, include the warehouse image that shows it and the listing evidence for the ordered option. A short, organized record helps distinguish the seller's description from what was actually selected and what was actually received.

Choose evidence that answers the disputed point. An incorrect size label needs a clear label photo and the selected-size record. A missing accessory needs evidence of the included components and the received contents. A color complaint may require clarification because lighting affects appearance. Do not describe a hidden defect as confirmed merely because a photograph looks unusual. State what you observed and what still needs checking.

sections.heading: Separate cancellation from a completed return
paragraphs: Before seller dispatch, your question may concern whether the purchase can still be cancelled. After dispatch, a return may require receiving and sending the item back through an approved process. Do not assume that a cancellation request stops a carrier shipment already underway. Ask for the status of the request itself and distinguish requested, accepted, returned and refunded in your record.

A useful message identifies the order and asks whether cancellation is still possible at its current stage, what amount is expected to be refunded and whether any costs remain. If dispatch has already occurred, ask which procedure replaces cancellation. This avoids a common misunderstanding: treating the moment you submit a request as the moment the seller has agreed or the money has already been credited.

sections.heading: Review warehouse problems before parcel submission
paragraphs: The warehouse stage is a useful opportunity to examine available images and clarify a mismatch before committing to international delivery. Compare the received item with the chosen variant and your written purchase brief. If a material question remains, keep it visible in your notes and ask how to pause the relevant next step while the issue is reviewed. Do not assume that writing a message automatically places an operational hold on the item.

For an illustrative example, suppose a jacket was ordered in black size L but the warehouse label shows size M. The enquiry should include both records and ask for the available correction or return process. It should not begin with an unsupported claim about fraud or demand an invented deadline. If the photographs are inconclusive, ask for the missing view before describing the mismatch as established.

sections.heading: Ask for the refund components separately
paragraphs: Record the item amount, domestic delivery, any purchasing service charge, selected inspection or photo services and any proposed return shipping or handling cost. These amounts may have different treatment. Request a breakdown of what is refundable, what has already been performed, what additional payment is required and what remains uncertain. Avoid treating the original order total as an automatic refund entitlement.

Use a hypothetical budget to see why the distinction matters. If an order had a $30 item amount, $2 domestic delivery and $1 of optional services, its total would be $33. A proposed refund of $30 does not explain the treatment of the other $3 or any return cost. Those figures are arithmetic examples in USD, not Superbuy prices. Ask for the actual ledger entries before accepting or disputing the calculation.

sections.heading: Keep seller approval and payment reconciliation distinct
paragraphs: An accepted return, carrier delivery back to a seller, a refund entry in your account and a withdrawal to a payment method are separate events. Track whichever of these apply to your case. Do not infer that every stage has completed because one message uses the word processed. Copy the exact account wording and ask which financial entry confirms that money has become available to you.

When checking a payment, record the amount and currency shown, the transaction date and the associated order or service reference. If you later move account funds through an available withdrawal method, review that method's current conditions separately. This guide does not promise an original-payment-method refund or a universal processing time. A transaction record and a clearly identified outstanding step are more reliable than a deadline taken from an unrelated customer's case.

sections.heading: Treat special listings and services individually
paragraphs: Before buying, inspect any displayed limitations associated with the source listing or service. A custom option, a used item, a preorder or a purchase from a less familiar marketplace should prompt specific questions about what happens if the seller cannot supply the intended product. Do not infer return eligibility merely because a different listing or a different marketplace previously allowed a return.

Ask those questions before committing when the answer would change your decision. Save the response with the listing record. If a restriction appears only after payment, document where it was shown and ask how it applies to your exact order. This approach does not establish legal rights or replace applicable consumer rules; it helps keep the platform conversation specific enough to resolve the operational question without inventing a universal policy.

sections.heading: Keep a chronological case log
paragraphs: Use one timeline for request submission, agent replies, seller decisions, any return dispatch, any confirmed receipt and the financial adjustment. Include the next agreed action and who is expected to perform it. If a message supplies an expected date, record it as an expectation from that message rather than converting it into a guaranteed deadline. Follow up with the existing case context when the stated next step has not appeared.

A concise follow-up might identify the order, summarize the last confirmed event and ask whether a particular action has completed. Repeated messages without new evidence can make a case harder to read. If the issue changes, explain the change explicitly. For example, a case that began as a size mismatch may become a question about the return carrier record or the refund breakdown; those require different supporting details.

sections.heading: Decide from the remaining cost and uncertainty
paragraphs: Before choosing between keeping an item, seeking a correction and requesting a return, compare the actual available options. Consider the documented mismatch, the cost of any proposed solution, the time constraints displayed in the account and whether the unresolved issue matters to your intended use. Treat this as your own decision framework, not as a recommendation to accept a defect or abandon an eligible claim.

Close the case only after the requested outcome and the financial record agree. Save the final decision, any relevant tracking and the refund or fee entries. Then update your product and parcel notes so the same item is not accidentally included in a shipping plan or counted twice in the budget. A clear record cannot guarantee acceptance, but it makes the next conversation more precise and helps prevent avoidable confusion about what was requested and what actually happened.

title: Superbuy Fees Explained: Product Cost, Services and Shipping
dek: Build a clear Superbuy budget by separating product payments, optional services, international shipping deposits and final adjustments.

sections.heading: Build a delivered-cost budget before choosing a product
paragraphs: Superbuy fees are easier to understand when you organize them by the decision that creates them. The product amount belongs to the purchase decision. Domestic delivery gets the order toward the warehouse. Optional services respond to a specific inspection or packing need. International delivery concerns the finished parcel and its selected route. One attractive product price cannot describe all of those stages. Keep an unconfirmed-cost column beside the total, and make clear which amounts have already been paid. This prevents a temporary estimate from being mistaken for a complete purchase budget when someone else reviews your shortlist.

The official Fee Structure and Shopping Agent guide describe purchasing and international shipping as separate stages. Use that structure to build your own budget, while checking the live account for the actual amounts applicable to the source marketplace and services you select. This article provides a comparison method and hypothetical USD examples. It does not publish a fixed shipping tariff, an exchange-rate promise or a universal all-in price.

sections.heading: Record the exact variant and the first payment
paragraphs: Start with the current seller listing and the selected option, not a category thumbnail or the lowest price in a range. Save the color, size, version, quantity and item amount. If a listing contains both a complete product and an accessory, confirm that the displayed amount belongs to the product you intend to order. A spreadsheet row is a useful discovery reference, but the live option determines the purchase.

Add domestic shipping separately and note whether the amount applies to one item, a group of items or the seller order. Record any purchasing fee shown for that source or service. Do not assume that a statement about standard purchasing applies to every marketplace, used-item service or special request. Before confirming payment, the amount on your own order screen should be explainable as a set of line items.

sections.heading: Give optional services a specific purpose
paragraphs: A paid photo or inspection request should answer a question that could change your decision. For example, a chest-width measurement may help resolve a clothing-size uncertainty, while a close image of a connector can clarify a visible model detail. Buying extra pictures without knowing what you need to see can increase the order cost without producing useful evidence. Define the question before choosing the service.

Treat product services and parcel services as different categories in your budget. One concerns an individual received item; the other concerns the later shipment. Record the service name, quantity, displayed charging unit and total. When a screen shows a price per item, per order or per parcel, do not silently convert those into the same unit. The unit matters as much as the headline price when several products are involved.

sections.heading: Compare shipping estimates using the same inputs
paragraphs: A useful comparison keeps destination, item restrictions, expected packed dimensions and weight consistent. If one estimate assumes a shoe box and another removes it, the difference cannot be attributed entirely to the shipping line. Record what changed between scenarios. The official shipping calculator asks for destination, weight, dimensions and item characteristics; your saved estimate should preserve those inputs so the result can be interpreted later.

Read each available route's current conditions and fee breakdown. A low figure may not describe an eligible route for your actual contents or parcel shape. Do not choose a line solely from an old screenshot, another customer's weight or a price-per-kilogram claim. Keep the estimate date and the assumptions beside the amount. Recheck when warehouse measurements and the final packing plan replace your earlier guesses.

sections.heading: Separate the shipping deposit from the settled amount
paragraphs: The first international shipping payment is an estimate-based deposit in Superbuy's published purchasing workflow. Final parcel measurements and the logistics calculation can produce an adjustment. In your ledger, give the deposit, any later additional payment and any credited difference separate entries. That keeps cash already paid visible without counting it twice when the final cost becomes available.

A simple illustrative reconciliation is a $40 deposit followed by a $5 credit, leaving $35 as the shipping amount for that example. If an additional $4 were required instead, the result would be $44. These are hypothetical calculations, not route prices or predictions. Keep optional services and any separately charged destination amount in their own rows rather than assuming that one adjustment settles every component of the delivered cost.

sections.heading: Use a worked USD example without treating it as a quote
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical budget with two product amounts of $24 and $18, domestic delivery of $3, optional services of $2 and a final international shipping amount of $35. The total of those listed components is $82. If destination charges or payment-related costs have not yet been verified, label them unconfirmed; do not enter zero merely to make the total appear complete.

Now change one assumption. Suppose keeping retail packaging adds $6 to the final shipping estimate in this example. The comparable budget becomes $88 for the listed components, provided everything else stays the same. The question is whether that packaging is worth the difference to you. A scenario table makes the trade-off visible. It is much more useful than claiming that removing every box always saves a particular percentage.

sections.heading: Reconcile currency and payment records
paragraphs: Keep the currency displayed for each transaction alongside your USD planning column. If the source amount is in another currency, record the actual conversion used or label the USD figure as an estimate. Do not present a rounded conversion as an official Superbuy tariff. Your payment provider and the platform may show different stages of the transaction, so compare equivalent records before deciding that an unexplained fee exists.

Separate money added to an account from money spent on a particular order. A top-up can fund several purchases and should not be counted as the cost of every one of them. Reconcile the account balance, order debits and any refund entries. For payment fees or exchange-rate questions, use the current checkout and provider terms. An old community post cannot establish the amount charged on your present transaction.

sections.heading: Compare consolidation with realistic parcel alternatives
paragraphs: A single combined parcel may reduce repeated packaging or initial shipment charges, but it can also alter dimensions and route eligibility. Compare the actual alternatives you could choose: one combined parcel, two compatible groups or shipping ready items while a delayed order remains unresolved. Use the same product list and make any excluded item obvious. Otherwise a cheaper scenario may simply contain fewer goods.

Include the effect of waiting. Record storage deadlines and any currently applicable storage or extension costs before assuming that a later combined parcel is better value. Also distinguish financial savings from the risk of damage or the value of keeping original packaging. The best option is the one that meets your requirements at an understandable total, not necessarily the scenario with the smallest amount on a single line.

sections.heading: Finish with a budget you can audit
paragraphs: Before paying, verify the selected variants, quantities, domestic delivery and any purchasing services. Before submitting a parcel, verify the stored items, packaging choices, eligible route and shipping deposit. After dispatch, reconcile the final shipping entry and any adjustments. These three checkpoints help keep a changing order understandable without pretending that the first estimate can predict every later charge.

Keep your original assumptions after you learn the final result. Record which changes came from additional products, altered packaging, measurement differences, optional services or a different route. That history becomes a useful reference for your next purchase, while remaining specific to the parcel you actually sent. A careful budget does not eliminate uncertainty; it shows which amounts are known, which are estimated and which still need confirmation before the next commitment.

title: Superbuy Warehouse Storage: Deadlines, Fees and Extensions
dek: Plan Superbuy warehouse storage around each item's arrival record, free-storage window, extension conditions and realistic parcel decisions.

sections.heading: Give every stored item its own timeline
paragraphs: Superbuy warehouse storage is most useful when you treat it as a dated planning window for each item. Orders from different sellers can arrive at different times, so a shared haul does not necessarily have a single storage clock. Start with the warehouse record for each order and save its arrival information, the deadline or remaining days displayed in the account and any unresolved inspection or after-sales issue.

The aim is to make an intentional decision before a deadline becomes urgent. You may be waiting for another seller, a measurement, a return decision or enough compatible items to submit a parcel. Write down which of those reasons applies. An item marked simply waiting can remain overlooked even after the original reason has disappeared. A clear reason and a next review date make the warehouse list easier to manage.

sections.heading: Check the published policy and the live order together
paragraphs: Superbuy's Fee Structure reviewed on 6 October 2026 describes 90 days of free storage, a subsequent daily charge of CN¥0.1 per item and a standard maximum storage period of 180 days. It also describes a paid extension service that extends the maximum period without resetting the free-storage allowance. Treat those as the published baseline at the review date and verify the terms and dates displayed for your particular item before relying on them.

Do not calculate an official deadline solely from the date you paid the seller. Purchasing and warehouse arrival are different stages. If your account shows a date or remaining-day count that you cannot reconcile, ask for clarification while there is time to act. Save the reply with the item record. Public guidance can explain the policy, but it cannot resolve an individual account discrepancy from outside your order.

sections.heading: Separate free storage from maximum storage
paragraphs: The end of free storage is a cost checkpoint; the maximum storage limit is a different operational deadline. Paying a daily storage charge does not by itself prove that an item may remain indefinitely. Similarly, buying an extension should not be interpreted as a new free-storage period unless the live terms explicitly say so. Keep separate fields for free-storage expiry, maximum deadline and any approved extension.

A practical worksheet can also include the item value, reason for waiting and next action. For instance, a stored hoodie may be waiting for a second garment, while a shoe order may be waiting for a measurement. Those are different blockers and may need different responses. Reviewing both as merely unfinished orders hides the decision that would let each item move forward.
